title: 21st Century Boys
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A two-volume coda to 20th Century Boys. After the cult leader 'Friend' dies, Kenji Endo and his niece Kanna race to stop a final bomb plot while UN forces move into Tokyo. Kenji enters the cult's virtual-reality simulation of his 1970s childhood, where he confronts his younger self and the small cruelties and guilt that shaped the man who became Friend.
life_message: It holds up facing one's past honestly and taking responsibility for small wrongs before they grow into great ones.

content.note: Climax of a saga of bombings, virus attacks and assassinations; a final battle over a world-ending bomb (Wikipedia on the parent series; Fandom Post; AniList Military 72%, Tragedy 79%).
Doomsday-cult conspiracy, ghost and memory scenes, threat of global destruction (Wikipedia; AniList Conspiracy 91%, Cult 86%, Ghost 79%).
The boys' childhood hideout held stolen adult magazines in the parent series (Wikipedia); little else noted (to verify).
Viz T+ / 16+ rating; profanity level not stated (ComicBookBin; Fandom Post; to verify).
Adult drinking possible; not noted in reviews (to verify).
Childhood isolation and guilt behind Friend's identity; a friend's reported suicide earlier in the saga (Wikipedia; Fandom Post). Detail to verify.
Childhood shoplifting and blame-shifting revisited as the root of later harm (to verify).
Live-action films exist for the parent series; no in-story product focus.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia reception praises plot, twists and characters; none calls it preachy (to verify)
delivery.note: Responsibility for small wrongs is carried by Kenji's return to his childhood, with uneasy sympathy for the boy who became Friend.

winners_losers: Ordinary friends who own their past win; the cult and its manufactured savior lose. Sympathy also extends, uneasily, to the forgotten child who became Friend.
